title: Old vs New Tax Regime: Compare for AY 2026–27
description: Compare the old and new Indian tax regimes for AY 2026–27 using official rules, eligible deductions, salary facts, and separate estimates before choosing.
lead: Last verified against the listed official sources on 28 October 2026. This guide explains a comparison process, not the tax result for an individual.
editorialFrame: There is no regime that is automatically better for every salaried person. The Income Tax Department says the old and new regimes have different rates and deductions, and asks taxpayers to compare their own position. For AY 2026–27, use the official year-specific rules and calculator, identify which deductions you can actually claim, and keep payroll withholding separate from the option you ultimately exercise in your return.

sections.heading: Start with the correct assessment year
sections.content:
Write down the financial year in which the income was earned and the assessment year for which the return is being filed. A slab, rebate, or deduction from another year can make a comparison wrong even if the calculator accepts the inputs. Use the official Income Tax Department material for the relevant year and confirm that the return instructions and tax calculator match it.

Keep prior-year figures only as a reference. Salary revisions, a job change, rent, investments, capital gains, and other income can all change the comparison. If your income includes business or professional income, the option process can differ from the salaried non-business case described here. Check the relevant official guidance before assuming you can change regimes in the same way each year.

sections.heading: List the facts before comparing regimes
sections.content:
Gather expected salary, taxable allowances, interest and other income, eligible deductions, exemptions, and any income that has a separate tax treatment. Use amounts you can support with statements or records rather than the maximum you hope to claim. Separate employer projections from amounts already paid. If a bonus or joining payment is uncertain, include it only in a clearly labelled scenario, not as guaranteed cash.

The Income Tax Department's FAQ explains that the old regime permits various deductions and exemptions while the new regime allows fewer. That does not tell you which regime is better for your facts. Mark each potential claim as eligible, documented, pending, or not applicable, and confirm category-specific conditions from official guidance before entering it into the comparison.

sections.heading: Run two like-for-like estimates
sections.content:
Use the same income, tax year, and household facts for both estimates. Change only the regime-specific items that the rules allow. Compare the final tax liability, not only the rate or the monthly TDS amount. Include applicable surcharge, cess, and other income in the official calculation where relevant. Keep a copy of the inputs so you can spot when a later estimate silently changes a number.

The official portal calculator is a useful cross-check, not a personalized assessment or guarantee of a refund. Compare its result with your own calculation only after checking the income year, regime, deductions, and return type. If results differ, identify the line that changed instead of selecting the lower figure without explanation. Ask a qualified tax professional about complex income or uncertain eligibility.

sections.heading: Understand default status and the filing choice
sections.content:
The Income Tax Department FAQ says the new regime is the default for the specified taxpayer categories, while eligible taxpayers may opt for the old regime. For non-business cases, the FAQ says the option may be exercised each year in the return by the due date. It also distinguishes an employer intimation for withholding from the option exercised in the income-tax return.

If your payroll team deducted tax using one regime, do not assume that automatically settles the return choice. Check the current return instructions and due date. People with business or professional income may have a different process and restrictions, including forms and timing described by the department. This guide focuses on a salaried non-business comparison and does not resolve every taxpayer's filing status.

sections.heading: Check claims and records before choosing
sections.content:
For every deduction or exemption in the old-regime estimate, identify the official condition and the record that supports it. For every salary component, check whether it is taxable and whether the employer's document describes a benefit or only a reimbursement. A salary calculator can estimate only what its inputs describe; it cannot decide whether a claim is legally available or whether a document proves it.

Keep rent receipts, investment or insurance proof, loan interest statements, salary slips, and any other relevant records in an organized folder. Do not create a claim to make one regime appear better. If you are unsure whether an item qualifies, leave it out of the confirmed scenario and ask a qualified adviser or consult the current official source.

sections.heading: Compare annual tax and monthly cash separately
sections.content:
Annual tax liability and monthly in-hand pay answer different questions. Payroll withholding can vary during the year, and an employer may use an estimated declaration that differs from the eventual return. Estimate take-home pay with the documented salary breakup and label it as an estimate. Keep employer PF, variable pay, reimbursements, and benefits distinct from cash that reaches your account.

A small annual tax difference may not matter as much as a large difference in deductions, benefits, or documentation effort for a particular person. Make your decision with the whole financial picture, not a dramatic headline about one regime. Revisit the estimate when your income, eligible claims, or tax-year rules change.

sections.heading: Keep an audit trail for the choice
sections.content:
Save the income figures, deductions, official calculator result, and source year used in your comparison. If you revise an input, note why. This makes it easier to explain a difference between an early payroll estimate and the return you later file. It also helps a tax professional review one assumption without rebuilding the entire calculation from memory.

Do not upload identity documents or sensitive tax records to an untrusted tool just to compare regimes. Use official services or a qualified adviser and retain only the records you need. If your circumstances change during the year, update the estimate rather than treating the first result as fixed.

sections.heading: Sources and verification date
sections.content:
Last verified against the listed official sources on 28 October 2026. The official FAQ says the new regime is the default, that the regimes differ in rates and deductions, and that comparison should reflect the taxpayer's circumstances. It also distinguishes employer withholding intimation from the return option.

The Income Tax Department page for salaried individuals is an overview and says it is not exhaustive. Use the current Act, rules, forms, notifications, and official calculator for your facts. The links below were checked for this guide; a future change in law or portal content may require a new comparison.

faqs.question: Which regime is better for salaried employees?
faqs.answer: It varies with income, eligible deductions, exemptions, and facts. Compare both using official year-specific inputs.

faqs.question: Does telling my employer choose my return regime?
faqs.answer: The Department FAQ distinguishes employer withholding intimation from the option exercised in the income-tax return.

faqs.question: Can I compare using last year's tax slabs?
faqs.answer: Use the rules for the correct assessment year. Prior-year figures can be a reference, not the current answer.

faqs.question: Should I include deductions I may claim later?
faqs.answer: Keep unverified claims out of the confirmed case until you check eligibility and the documents required.
